content:
# Sirach 21 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** Sirach 21 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 001 — 21:2 "destroy / slay / kill"
**Verse:** 21:2
**EMET:** "slaying the souls of men"
**LOGOS:** "destroying the souls of men"
**PNEUMA:** "it kills people outright"
**Issue:** ἀναιροῦσα — "taking up/away," i.e., killing. EMET preserves "souls" (ψυχάς); PNEUMA drops "souls" for natural English. SOPHIA retains "lives" as a compromise.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "destroying the lives of men" — "lives" captures ψυχάς without sounding archaic.

---

## Disagreement 002 — 21:7 "mighty in tongue / smooth talker / known for his tongue"
**Verse:** 21:7
**EMET:** "One-known-for-his-tongue is a-capable-man from-afar"
**LOGOS:** "A person mighty in tongue is known from afar"
**PNEUMA:** "You can spot a smooth talker from a mile away"
**Issue:** δυνατὸς ἐν γλώσσῃ — "powerful/capable in tongue." The proverb's meaning is ambiguous: is such a person admirable or dangerous? Context suggests both. PNEUMA's "smooth talker" introduces a negative connotation not clearly present.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A person mighty in speech is known from afar" — neutral, preserving ambiguity.

---

## Disagreement 003 — 21:8 "burial mound / winter-tomb / burial"
**Verse:** 21:8
**EMET:** "winter-tomb"
**LOGOS:** "burial mound"
**PNEUMA:** "winter grave"
**Issue:** χειμῶνος — "winter" or "storm." The image is of futile accumulation. EMET hyphenates to capture the compound feel. LOGOS reads "burial mound." SOPHIA selects "grave in winter" to preserve the seasonal dimension.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "his own grave in winter" — retains the seasonal/storm nuance.

---

## Disagreement 004 — 21:9 "tow / dry flax / tow gathered"
**Verse:** 21:9
**EMET:** "like tow-gathered-together"
**LOGOS:** "like gathered tow"
**PNEUMA:** "like a bundle of dry flax"
**Issue:** στυππεῖον συνηγμένον — "bundled tow." PNEUMA explains "tow" as "dry flax" for clarity. EMET and LOGOS retain "tow" as a technical term for the material.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "like tow bundled together" — retains the term, which is sufficiently understood.

---

## Disagreement 005 — 21:11 "controls / masters / keeps"
**Verse:** 21:11
**EMET:** "controls his thoughts"
**LOGOS:** "masters his own thoughts"
**PNEUMA:** "you master your own impulses"
**Issue:** κρατήσει διανοήματος — "will master/hold his thoughts." PNEUMA shifts to "impulses" (interpretive), while EMET/LOGOS stay closer to διανοήματος = "thoughts/reflections."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "masters his own thoughts" — literal and apt.

---

## Disagreement 006 — 21:11 "completion / fulfillment / crown"
**Verse:** 21:11b
**EMET:** "the completion of-the-fear-of-the-LORD is wisdom"
**LOGOS:** "the completion of the fear of the LORD is wisdom"
**PNEUMA:** "the crown of the fear of the LORD is wisdom itself"
**Issue:** συντέλεια — "completion/fulfillment/consummation." PNEUMA's "crown" is interpretive but vivid. SOPHIA chooses "fulfillment" as slightly richer than "completion."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "the fulfillment of the fear of the LORD is wisdom."

---

## Disagreement 007 — 21:14 "inner part / inner mind / mind"
**Verse:** 21:14
**EMET:** "The-inner-part of a-fool"
**LOGOS:** "The inner part of a fool"
**PNEUMA:** "The mind of a fool"
**Issue:** ἐγκάτου — "inner part/gut/belly." The visceral term is significant. PNEUMA generalizes to "mind." SOPHIA uses "inner mind" to bridge bodily and intellectual registers.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The inner mind of a fool" — captures both the physical and cognitive dimensions.

---

## Disagreement 008 — 21:15 "dissolute / self-indulgent / person"
**Verse:** 21:15
**EMET:** "the dissolute man"
**LOGOS:** "the self-indulgent man"
**PNEUMA:** "a self-indulgent person"
**Issue:** ἄκρατος — "unrestrained/intemperate." "Dissolute" is archaic; "self-indulgent" is more accessible. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "the self-indulgent man."

---

## Disagreement 009 — 21:16 "utterance / discourse / talk"
**Verse:** 21:16
**EMET:** "The-utterance of a-fool"
**LOGOS:** "The discourse of a fool"
**PNEUMA:** "A fool's talk"
**Issue:** στόμα — "mouth." EMET and LOGOS render by implication ("utterance/discourse"); PNEUMA renders as "talk." SOPHIA selects "discourse" as appropriately elevated for wisdom literature.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The discourse of a fool."

---

## Disagreement 010 — 21:20 "barely smiles quietly / smiles only quietly"
**Verse:** 21:20
**EMET:** "a-clever-man barely-smiles quietly"
**LOGOS:** "a clever man smiles only quietly"
**PNEUMA:** "a wise person smiles quietly, if at all"
**Issue:** μόλις — "scarcely/barely." The adverb qualifies the restraint. PNEUMA's "if at all" is interpretive addition. EMET's "barely-smiles" is vivid. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a clever man smiles only quietly."

---

## Disagreement 011 — 21:22 "stands-back-in-respect / holds back respectfully / waits"
**Verse:** 21:22
**EMET:** "stands-back-in-respect before it"
**LOGOS:** "holds back respectfully from entering"
**PNEUMA:** "waits respectfully at the threshold"
**Issue:** αἰσχυνθήσεται — "will be ashamed/show respect." The verb indicates shame-modesty, not mere politeness. EMET and LOGOS capture this better. PNEUMA's "threshold" is an addition.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "a person of experience stands back respectfully."

---

## Disagreement 012 — 21:24 "boorishness / ill-bred / low behavior"
**Verse:** 21:24
**EMET:** "It-is-boorishness in a-person"
**LOGOS:** "It is ill-bred"
**PNEUMA:** "Listening at doors is low behavior"
**Issue:** ἀπαιδευσία — "lack of education/boorishness." EMET's "boorishness" is closest. LOGOS's "ill-bred" is idiomatic. PNEUMA paraphrases. SOPHIA retains "the mark of a boor" to keep the social-status dimension.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "It is the mark of a boor to eavesdrop at the door."

---

## Disagreement 013 — 21:26 heart/mouth inversion rendering
**Verse:** 21:26
**EMET:** "In-the-mouth of-the-foolish is their-heart, but the-heart of-the-wise is in-their-mouth"
**LOGOS:** "The heart of fools is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart"
**PNEUMA:** "For a fool, the mouth runs ahead of the heart; for the wise, the heart governs the mouth"
**Issue:** The Greek antithesis is precise: ἐν στόματι / ἐν καρδίᾳ. PNEUMA interprets. EMET and LOGOS preserve the tighter parallelism. SOPHIA follows LOGOS exactly.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "The heart of fools is on their lips, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart" — slight adjustment to "lips" (more natural in English) vs "mouth."

---

## Disagreement 014 — 21:28 "whisperer / gossip"
**Verse:** 21:28
**EMET:** "A-whisperer defiles his-own-soul"
**LOGOS:** "A whisperer defiles his own soul"
**PNEUMA:** "The gossip poisons their own soul"
**Issue:** ψιθυριστής — "whisperer/gossip." PNEUMA's "poisons" for μολυνεῖ ("defiles") is interpretive. "Defiles" is the more literal and liturgically resonant term. SOPHIA follows LOGOS/EMET on "defiles" but uses "gossip" for readability.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA: "A gossip defiles his own soul."
